Note::to_utf8_strict¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::to_utf8_strict() const

Promote Bytes To Text, Rejecting Anything Not Valid UTF-8¶

to_utf8_strict() re-tags a bytes-mode Note as UTF-8 text without changing a single byte — but only after checking that every cell already contains well-formed UTF-8. If any cell does not, the call raises pluss::Error and no result is produced. Use it at a trust boundary, when you have a bytes payload that is supposed to be UTF-8 and you want a hard failure rather than silent corruption if it is not.

What “valid” means¶

Each cell is scanned as a sequence of UTF-8 code units: a lead byte in the 0x00–0x7F, 0xC0–0xDF, 0xE0–0xEF, or 0xF0–0xF7 range followed by the right number of 0x80–0xBF continuation bytes. A stray continuation byte, a truncated multi-byte sequence, or a 0xFF produces the rejection. Validation runs over the whole Note before any result is built, so the operation is all-or-nothing.

Called on a Note that is already text, it validates and returns an equivalent text Note. The result is shape-preserving and shares the input’s byte content exactly.

For a version that never fails — substituting the replacement character for each bad sequence — use to_utf8_lossy. To interpret non-UTF-8 bytes in a known legacy encoding instead of rejecting them, use from_latin1 or from_windows1252.

Example 1: Clean Bytes Become Text¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::bytes({"café", "abc"}).to_utf8_strict())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["café", "abc"]

The bytes are unchanged; only the encoding tag flips from bytes to utf8.

Example 2: Invalid Bytes Are Rejected¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes({std::string("bad\xFF\xFE") + "bytes"}).to_utf8_strict();
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

Note::to_utf8_strict found invalid UTF-8 payload

See Also¶

  • Note::to_utf8_lossy: the non-failing counterpart.

  • Note::from_latin1 / Note::from_windows1252: decode legacy single-byte encodings into text.

  • Note::is_utf8_valid: test validity per cell instead of raising.
